figures.alt: A sugar cube sitting in a glass of clear water, with white specks spreading out from it into the water.
figures.caption: A sugar cube spreads out into the water as it dissolves. Once it has dissolved, the sugar is still in the water, in tiny pieces too small to see.

figures.alt: A science table with sand mixed with iron filings in a bowl, a magnet in a plastic bag pulling up the filings, a funnel with filter paper over a cup, and a dark plate with white salt crystals.
figures.caption: The separation kit: a magnet for iron, water and a filter for sand, and drying to get the salt back.

figures.alt: Three kids at a science table separating a mixture: one holds a magnet in a plastic bag, one pours water, and one holds a funnel steady over a cup.
figures.caption: Separating a mixture takes steps: a magnet for iron, water to dissolve the salt, and a filter for the sand.

figures.alt: Four panels left to right. Mix: sand and salt on the table by a cup of water. Stir: the water is clear and the sand has settled on the bottom. Filter: sand stays on the filter paper and clear salt water drips into the cup below. Evaporate: white salt crystals are left in a dish.
figures.caption: Four steps, left to right. 1 Mix: sand and salt in a cup of water. 2 Stir: the salt disappears into the water, and the sand settles on the bottom. 3 Filter: the sand stays on the filter paper, and clear salt water drips into the cup below. 4 Evaporate (the water turns into invisible gas and leaves): white salt crystals stay in the dish. Dissolved salt is not gone. Filtering takes out the sand, and evaporating brings the salt back.

figures.alt: Interactive: twenty particles move as a solid, liquid or gas, and a temperature slider changes their speed but not their size.
figures.caption: Watch 20 particles in a solid, a liquid, and a gas, and heat them.

figures.alt: Interactive: step through mixing, stirring, filtering and evaporating salt and sand, with a zoom view that shows the dissolved salt bits.
figures.caption: Mix, stir, filter, and evaporate. Then zoom in on the salt to see that it is still there.

figures.alt: Grouped bar graph of sample mass in grams (not measured). Sealed cup of ice melting: 82 before, 82 after. Sealed bag with baking soda and vinegar: 45 before, 45 after. Each pair is the same height.
figures.caption: Sample data (not measured): mass before and after. The sealed cup of melting ice stays 82 g (about 3 ounces). The sealed bag with baking soda and vinegar stays 45 g (about 1 1/2 ounces). Each pair of bars is the same height: matter did not disappear.
